transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you’re here. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure on my house is just... you know, regular paperwork and missed payments. Which is completely false. Speaking of paperwork, you wouldn't believe the stack of inventory sheets I have to sign off on at the store every single week. I supervise the sales floor, and the new cashiers they hire, they don't even know how to load the receipt tape anymore. I had this one girl last week, she jammed the main register three times before her lunch break. It's just exhausting trying to manage people who don't pay attention. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Right, the house. The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job—probably the ones messing up the registers on purpose—they’ve been quietly working together to push me out of my house. They think I don't know what's going on. And no amount of papers they try to show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes for almost two years now. Two years... I actually planted these really beautiful hydrangeas in the front yard two years ago, right when all this started. They need a lot of water, hydrangeas do. If you don't water them every morning in the summer, they just wilt right down to the dirt.
Have you had any periods of feeling unusually high, energized, or needing much less sleep than usual?

High or energized? No, not at all. I sleep my normal amount, really. Well, unless I have coffee too late in the day. I actually had to stop drinking it after lunch because they changed the brand we get in the breakroom at work. That same girl who keeps jamming the registers, she’s the one who orders the breakroom supplies now, and she buys this cheap dark roast that just tastes like burnt dirt. 

I told the store manager we should just get one of those single-cup pod machines. My sister has one in her kitchen and she swears by it, but honestly, I think those little plastic cups are awful for the environment. Have you seen those documentaries about the plastic in the ocean? It's just terrible what we're doing to the sea turtles. They think the plastic bags are jellyfish, so they eat them. I tried to switch to only reusable canvas bags at the grocery store, but I always forget them in the trunk of my car. Then I end up having to buy more of them at the checkout, so now I have like thirty canvas bags just sitting in my hallway... wait, what did you ask me about? Oh, sleep. Yeah, no, my sleep is completely normal.
Have you ever heard voices that other people could not hear?

Voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. Just the normal sounds of the store, really. Though lately, the intercom system at work has been making this awful buzzing sound. It's like a low hum, right over the shoe department. I told maintenance about it three weeks ago, but you know how they are. They just put a work order in the system and then it sits there forever. 

Speaking of shoes, it is so hard to find a good pair of comfortable flats when you're on your feet for eight hours a day. I used to buy these memory foam ones, but they discontinued the style. Isn't that always how it goes? You find something you really like, something that actually works, and then some corporate office somewhere decides to just stop making it. They did the same thing with my favorite brand of toothpaste last year. I had to go to four different pharmacies just to buy up whatever they had left on the shelves. The pharmacist at the one on Elm Street—he’s a nice guy, always wears these really bright bow ties—he said they do that just to force people to buy the newer, more expensive versions. Which makes sense, honestly. It's all just about money with these companies. But anyway, no, I've never heard any voices or anything like that.
Have you ever believed that people were sending you special messages or signals meant just for you?

Special messages? No, I don't think so. I mean, people don't really send messages much anymore anyway, do they? It's all text messages now. My niece texts me all the time, mostly just pictures of her cat. It's a Maine Coon, you know, those really huge fluffy ones? He takes up almost the entire couch when he stretches out. She bought him this little harness so she can take him on walks, which I think is just ridiculous. Cats aren't dogs, they don't want to be walked down the sidewalk. 

I saw someone walking a ferret once, over by the park near my house. It was on this tiny little neon pink leash. I didn't even know you could keep ferrets in the city. Aren't they illegal in some places? I remember reading something about that in a magazine at the dentist's office. Speaking of the dentist, I really need to reschedule my cleaning. My hygienist retired last month—she was wonderful, she always gave me extra of those little travel flosses. The new girl they hired just seems so rushed. She poked my gums twice last time. It's so hard to find good help these days, just like at the store. But um... what were you asking about? Oh, signals. No, no one is sending me any special signals or anything. Just normal texts and emails.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually irritable or agitated for several days in a row?

Irritable? Agitated? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I get annoyed sometimes, but who doesn't? Like the other day, I was at the gas station—the one on the corner of 4th and Main, with the really bright LED sign that flashes the prices? They changed the sign so it flashes every three seconds now, and it is so distracting when you're trying to turn left there. 

Anyway, I went inside to pay because the card reader at the pump was broken. Again. It feels like those machines are always broken. And the guy in front of me was buying scratch-off tickets, but not just one or two. He stood there scratching them right at the counter, and then buying more with whatever he won. He must have been there for ten minutes. I don't understand the appeal of those things, honestly. The odds are so terrible. My uncle used to buy them every Friday after work. He kept all the losing ones in a shoebox in his closet for some reason. I helped my aunt clean out his house after he passed away, and we found like... five shoeboxes just full of losing lottery tickets. It took us all afternoon to recycle them all. The recycling truck in my neighborhood comes so early now, too. If I don't put the bin out the night before, I always miss it. And then the wind catches the lid and blows it open... wait, did you ask about being irritable? Yeah, no, I don't get agitated like that for days in a row or anything. Just normal annoyances, you know?
Have you ever believed that other people could read your thoughts?

Read my thoughts? Oh, goodness, no. That sounds like something out of one of those science fiction movies my brother used to watch. He was obsessed with all that stuff—aliens, mind reading, time travel. He had this massive collection of VHS tapes in his bedroom, all perfectly alphabetized. It was the only organized thing about him, honestly. His room was always a disaster zone. My mother used to threaten to go in there with a snow shovel just to clear a path to his bed. 

She was always very particular about cleanliness, my mother. Every Saturday morning, she'd have us up at 7 AM scrubbing baseboards. I hated it then, but I guess it rubbed off on me because I cannot stand a messy house now. Even at the store, I drive my staff crazy making sure all the displays are perfectly aligned. The new seasonal endcaps went up yesterday, and they had the autumn wreaths hanging all crooked. It drives me absolutely up the wall when things aren't symmetrical. I had to stay an hour late just to fix them. And of course, the AC was acting up again, so it was sweltering in there. I don't know why corporate insists on controlling the thermostat remotely from three states away. It makes no sense. If the people actually in the building are sweating, shouldn't we be able to turn the air up? But, no, no one can read my thoughts. I don't think that's even possible.
Has this belief that the bank and people at work are working together to push you out of your house affected any other part of your life, like your relationships or your ability to work?

Well, I mean... it definitely makes things tense at home. My husband and I, we can't even talk about the foreclosure notices without it turning into a huge argument. He just doesn't see what's right in front of him. We used to never argue, honestly. When we first got married, we had this little apartment over on Elm Street, right above a bakery. Oh, the smell of fresh bread every morning was just incredible. They made these blueberry scones that were out of this world. I tried making them at home once, but they turned out like little hockey pucks. Baking is such an exact science, you know? You can't just throw things in a bowl like you can with a soup or a stew. I make a really good beef stew in the slow cooker. I put carrots, potatoes, pearl onions... the trick is to sear the beef first before you put it in. 

But anyway, yeah, the arguments. It's just exhausting. And at work, it's spilling over too. I've had a few really tense exchanges with the managers lately over just ordinary paperwork. They keep asking me to sign these forms, and I know what they're doing, so I push back. Now everyone is walking on eggshells around me. I'm still doing my job, I'm still working, but people are definitely more careful when they talk to me. Which is fine, I guess. I just wish they'd stop acting like I don't know what's going on. Like with the new employee handbook they handed out last week. They changed the font size, and I know it was just to squeeze in new clauses without us noticing. I spent three hours comparing it to the old one. My eyes were crossing by the end of it. I really need to get my prescription checked, actually. My glasses keep slipping down my nose, the little screws on the side are loose. I tried fixing it with one of those tiny screwdrivers from a glasses repair kit, but the screw just stripped. Those kits are so cheap nowadays.
Do your thoughts ever feel jumbled or hard to follow, as if your mind is jumping around in a way that makes it hard for other people to understand you?

Jumbled? No, I don't think my thoughts are jumbled at all. I mean, everything I say makes perfect sense to me. I'm just trying to explain the whole picture, you know? Like when you're putting together a puzzle, you can't just look at one piece and know what the whole thing is. You need all the pieces. I love puzzles, actually. My grandmother and I used to do those big 1,000-piece ones on her dining room table. She had this beautiful mahogany table that she kept covered with a plastic tablecloth so it wouldn't get scratched. We'd sit there for hours on Sunday afternoons. She always smelled like lavender and those little peppermint candies she kept in her purse. 

I still buy those peppermints sometimes, just for the nostalgia. They're getting harder to find, though. The grocery store down the street stopped carrying them. They rearranged the whole candy aisle last month, and now I can't find anything. It's so frustrating when they do that. You get used to a routine, knowing exactly where everything is, and then they just upend it all. Like at the bank, they keep changing the tellers. Every time I go in, it's a new face, someone who doesn't know me, someone who's probably been briefed on what to say to me. It's so obvious what they're doing. But no, my thoughts aren't hard to follow. People understand me just fine, they just don't want to listen to what I'm actually saying.
Has this belief caused you to stop working or to withdraw from other parts of your life?

Withdraw? Stop working? No, I haven't stopped working. I mean, I still get up every morning, put on my uniform, and go in to supervise my team. I handle the schedules, I deal with the customer complaints... which, by the way, have been ridiculous lately. This one woman yelled at me for ten minutes yesterday because we didn't have the specific brand of organic dog shampoo she wanted. I told her we don't even carry pet supplies, we're a home goods store, but she just wouldn't listen. People are so entitled these days. It reminds me of my cousin's wedding. She had this massive fit because the florist used ivory roses instead of pure white. She actually threw a vase at the wall. It was a beautiful vase, too, cut glass, probably cost a fortune. I love cut glass. I have this gorgeous bowl on my dining table that I found at an antique shop in Vermont. We went there for our honeymoon, actually. The leaves were just starting to turn, all those brilliant reds and oranges. It was breathtaking. We stayed in this little bed and breakfast where they made fresh maple syrup. 

But anyway, no, I haven't withdrawn from life. I still take care of myself, I still do my job. The only time things get really difficult or I feel like I can't function is when the foreclosure stuff comes up. Like if I get a piece of mail from the bank, or they call, or if there's some new paperwork at work that I know is tied to them trying to take the house. That's when I have to stop and deal with it, because it's all connected. But if that's not happening, I'm just doing my normal routine. Like grocery shopping. I still go every Sunday. Although, I really need to find a new store, because like I said, they moved the peppermints, and now they've stopped carrying my favorite brand of coffee filters. The cone-shaped ones, you know? The basket ones just fold over and make a mess in the machine. It's impossible to get a good cup of coffee if the filter collapses.
Have you ever had any hallucinations, like hearing voices or seeing things that other people could not?

Voices? Seeing things? No, no, I don't have anything like that. I mean, my hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, it's better than fine, I've always had really sensitive ears. When I was a kid, I could hear the ice cream truck when it was still three blocks away. My mom used to say I had bat ears. I loved getting those strawberry shortcake bars, the ones with the little crunchy bits on the outside? They were so good. They don't taste the same anymore, though. I bought a box last summer when it was really hot, and the crunchy part was all soggy. It's like they changed the recipe to save money. Everyone is cutting corners these days. Just like the city with the streetlights on our block. They replaced the bulbs with these awful LED ones that buzz. Do you hear that buzzing sometimes? It drives me crazy when I'm trying to sleep. I had to buy a white noise machine, but it only has these weird settings like 'babbling brook' or 'summer night.' The summer night one has crickets, and who wants to sleep listening to crickets? It just makes me think there are bugs in the house. But no, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I see exactly what's going on.
Have you ever felt that this belief about the bank and your coworkers was definitely, unquestionably true even when other people tried to convince you it wasn’t?

Unquestionably true? Yes, absolutely. I mean, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... just paperwork and missed payments, like it's some normal administrative thing. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. 

Speaking of papers, though, the documents they use at the bank are always printed on that really thick, heavy stock. We used to use paper like that for the promotional signage at my store, back before corporate made us switch to digital displays. I really hate the digital displays. The brightness gives me a headache, and the colors are never right. The red always looks a little bit orange, you know? Like a burnt sienna. I had a crayon that exact color when I was little, in the big box of 64 with the sharpener built into the back. I used to color for hours on the living room floor. My mom had this thick, green shag carpet, the kind you could lose a quarter in if you dropped it. My brother and I used to pretend it was a jungle for my plastic dinosaurs. The triceratops was always my favorite. I had a green one and a purple one, but the dog chewed up the purple one's tail. He was a golden retriever named Buster. Best dog we ever had, honestly. He used to wait for me by the front window every day after school.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more withdrawn from other people than you used to be?

Withdrawn? From other people? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still talk to people. I have to talk to people all day at work. But I guess I don't go out as much as I used to. It's just exhausting, you know? Dealing with everyone. Plus, going out costs so much money now. Have you seen the price of a movie ticket lately? It's outrageous. And the popcorn! They charge you like ten dollars for a bucket of popcorn, and they don't even use real butter anymore. It's some kind of weird, yellow oil. I remember when I was a teenager, I worked at the local theater for a summer. We had this big block of actual butter that we'd melt down. The smell was incredible. It would just permeate your clothes, though. I'd come home smelling like a walking concession stand. My mom used to make me leave my uniform in the garage because she said it was making the whole house smell like a carnival. We had this old, detached garage with a creaky wooden door. My dad spent a whole weekend trying to fix the track on that door once, but he ended up just making it worse. He was always trying to fix things himself instead of calling a professional. He tried to fix the plumbing under the kitchen sink once and ended up flooding the entire kitchen. The water ruined the linoleum. It was this awful, 70s-style yellow and brown pattern anyway, so I guess it was a blessing in disguise. But we had to eat takeout for a week while they replaced the floor. We got Chinese food from this place down the street, Golden Dragon. They had the best egg rolls. So crispy. But anyway, no, I don't think I'm withdrawn. I just prefer to stay home where it's quiet.
Have you had any times when your mood was unusually depressed or very high around the same time this foreclosure belief was strongest?

Depressed? Or high? No, no, my mood's been pretty normal, I think. I mean, as normal as you can be when people are actively trying to steal your home from you. But I haven't been like, crying in bed all day or bouncing off the walls. I've just been focused. You have to be focused when you're dealing with something like this. Speaking of focus, though, it's so hard to concentrate at work lately because they keep changing the layout of the store. Corporate sends down these new 'planograms' every month, and we have to move all the merchandise around. It's supposed to increase sales, but it just confuses the customers. Yesterday, this older lady spent twenty minutes looking for the travel-sized shampoo. We used to keep it right by the registers, which makes sense, right? People grab it on their way out. But now it's all the way in aisle four, next to the hair dye. I don't know who comes up with these ideas. Probably some guy in an office who's never actually worked retail a day in his life. My first retail job was at a pet store when I was in high school. I loved that job. I got to play with the puppies on my break. We had this one beagle mix, he had these huge floppy ears and he would just howl whenever the phone rang. It was the funniest thing. I wanted to adopt him so badly, but my mom said our house wasn't big enough for a dog. We lived in this little ranch-style house with a tiny backyard. The grass was always mostly crabgrass, no matter what my dad did to try and fix it. He bought all this expensive fertilizer and spent hours out there on the weekends, but it never looked like the lawns in the magazines. He was so proud of his lawnmower, though. It was a riding mower, bright red. He used to let me steer it when I was little, sitting on his lap. It smelled like gasoline and cut grass. I still love that smell. But anyway, no, my mood hasn't been unusually high or low. Just... dealing with things.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? Like hallucinations? No, no, I don't see things that aren't there. My eyesight is actually pretty good, considering I spend all day staring at those awful digital displays at work. I did have to get reading glasses last year, though. Just a mild prescription, but it makes a huge difference when I'm looking at the tiny print on the inventory sheets. I bought a pair of those cheap ones from the pharmacy, you know the ones that come in a three-pack? I got a blue pair, a red pair, and a tortoiseshell pair. The tortoiseshell ones are my favorite. They make me feel very... studious. Like a librarian. I always thought it would be nice to be a librarian. Just surrounded by books all day, quiet, organized. I used to go to the public library every Saturday when I was a kid. The children's section was in the basement, and it always smelled like old paper and floor wax. They had this big beanbag chair that was shaped like a hamburger. It was so faded and lumpy, but all the kids fought over who got to sit in it. I read all the Nancy Drew mysteries sitting in that hamburger chair. I loved Nancy Drew. She was so smart and independent, driving around in her blue roadster. I always wanted a convertible. Not blue, though. Maybe a cherry red one. With white leather seats. Although, white leather would be a nightmare to keep clean, especially if you spill coffee. I spilled coffee in my car just last week. It was one of those iced lattes, and it went right into the cup holder and got all sticky. I spent twenty minutes scrubbing it with a wet wipe, but it still smells like vanilla syrup in there. So, no, I don't see things. Just regular things.
Have there been times when you held this belief about the bank and your coworkers even though your mood felt completely normal?

Yeah, I mean, my mood is always normal when I'm thinking about it. Because it's just the reality of what's happening. The bank and my coworkers, they're always scheming, whether I'm feeling happy or sad or just... normal. Like right now, I feel totally fine. I had a good breakfast this morning. I made oatmeal. I usually buy the instant packets, you know, the maple brown sugar kind? But I decided to try making it from scratch with the rolled oats. It takes longer, obviously, but it's supposed to be healthier. I added some sliced almonds and a little bit of honey. I got the honey from this farmer's market I went to last weekend. It was so crowded there. People everywhere, pushing strollers and walking their dogs. There was this one guy selling artisan cheeses, and he had samples out. I tried this smoked gouda that was amazing, but it was like fifteen dollars for a tiny wedge. I can't justify spending that much on cheese. Not with the economy the way it is, and especially not with my job situation. My supervisor, she's been so nitpicky lately. Yesterday she got on my case because the endcap display for the seasonal candles wasn't perfectly symmetrical. Like anyone is going to notice if one pumpkin spice candle is slightly out of line. But she acts like it's a federal offense. I think she just likes to hear herself talk, honestly. She wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she moves her arms. You can hear her coming from three aisles away. It reminds me of my middle school math teacher, Mrs. Gable. She wore a lot of jewelry, too. And she always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She was so strict. If you didn't show your work on a math problem, she'd mark the whole thing wrong, even if you got the right answer. I hated math. I was always more of an English student. I loved writing essays. So, yeah, my mood is fine. The stuff with the bank is just... it's just a fact of my life right now.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when these beliefs were present only while your mood was very depressed or very high?

No, it's never been like that. It's not tied to being depressed or high, because I'm not either of those things. The situation with the bank is just always happening, regardless of my mood. I mean, my mood is pretty steady. Unless I haven't had my morning tea, I guess. I switched from coffee to green tea a few months ago because the acid in coffee was just killing my stomach. Plus, green tea has all those antioxidants. 

I buy the loose leaf kind from this little shop downtown. They have all these giant glass jars lining the walls, it looks like an old apothecary. The owner is this sweet older man who always gives me a free sample of a new blend. Last time he gave me this peach hibiscus one. It was bright pink when it brewed. It tasted a little like potpourri, honestly, but I drank it anyway. I hate wasting things. I'm the kind of person who will scrape the very bottom of the peanut butter jar with a spatula. My roommate in college used to just throw the jar away when there was still a good two tablespoons left! It drove me crazy. We did not get along very well. She was a theater major and was always doing vocal warm-ups at like, six in the morning. 'Red leather, yellow leather,' over and over. 

I was taking a lot of early classes so I was already awake, but still. I took this one art history class that was fascinating, though. We spent a whole month just on the Renaissance. The paintings from that era are so incredibly detailed. I always wonder how they got the fabric to look so realistic, like you could just reach out and touch the velvet. I have a velvet throw pillow on my couch, actually. It's emerald green. I got it on sale at HomeGoods. I love HomeGoods, you never know what you're going to find there. I went in for a picture frame once and came out with a giant ceramic owl. But anyway, no, my mood doesn't really have anything to do with what's going on.
Have you ever thought that some outside force is directly controlling your thoughts or actions?

Controlling my thoughts? No, no, I'm the one in charge of my own brain. Nobody is like... pulling strings or forcing me to do things. Well, except my store manager, but that's just her being a total micromanager. She tries to control everything I do on the floor. Like yesterday, she completely redid the associate schedule after I had already finalized it. And I had spent an hour color-coding it! 

I use those really nice gel pens, you know the ones that don't bleed through the paper? I have a set of thirty-six colors. I keep them in this little mesh pouch I found in the dollar spot at Target. Target is so dangerous, honestly. You go in for toothpaste and you come out with a new bathmat, three candles, and a bag of pretzels. I love those peanut butter filled pretzels. They're so salty and crunchy. I try not to buy them too often though, because I will literally sit on the couch and eat half the tub while watching HGTV. I love those home renovation shows. It's amazing how they can take a house that looks like a total dump and turn it into this beautiful open-concept thing in like, thirty minutes of television. I always want to knock down a wall in my apartment after I watch them, but I'm pretty sure my landlord would evict me. He's this grumpy guy who complains if you even put a nail in the wall to hang a picture. So I just use those Command hooks for everything. They really do work, as long as you pull the tab straight down when you take them off. If you pull it towards you, it rips the paint right off the drywall. I learned that the hard way in my last place. 

But yeah, no, my thoughts are just my own. No outside forces or anything like that.
Have you noticed a clear decline in your work performance because of these beliefs?

Well, no, not really a decline. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't involved, I still get up for work every day, I supervise my team, handle the schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself just fine. 

Like just yesterday, I had to deal with this woman trying to return a blender without a receipt. It didn't even have our store brand on it, but she was screaming at me that she bought it here. I just stayed calm, you know? Put on my customer service voice. I actually used to work in food service back when I was getting my associate's degree, and that really teaches you patience. People get so incredibly mad if you forget their extra ranch dressing. It's wild. The things people will yell over. 

But anyway, yeah, I do my job. The problems mostly just start when there's mail, or if the bank calls, or if the workplace paperwork seems tied to what I believe is happening with the house. Then it's... well, it's hard to ignore. 

Speaking of paperwork, our printer in the back office is always jamming. It’s this massive, ancient gray thing that sounds like an airplane taking off when it prints. I’ve put in like three maintenance requests for it, but corporate just tells us to clean the rollers with rubbing alcohol. Have you ever tried to reach inside a commercial printer? I always get black toner all over my hands and my cuffs. And it does not wash off easily. You have to scrub it with that gritty pumice soap, the orange kind mechanics use. My dad used to keep a giant bottle of that by the sink in the garage. He was always tinkering with his old Chevy truck. He loved that truck more than anything, I swear he waxed it every single Sunday afternoon... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my work. Yeah, my performance is totally fine as long as the bank and the house stuff isn't popping up in my paperwork.
During this time, have you also been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? No, I don't think so. I don't feel sad or down all day, if that's what you mean. I get up, I go to work, I do my thing. I mean, I have my moments of being annoyed, obviously, but not depressed. Like this morning, I was so annoyed because my neighbor decided to mow his lawn at 7 AM. Who does that on a weekday? And he has one of those gas mowers that sounds like a lawnmower and a chainsaw had a baby. It's so loud. 

I actually really want to get one of those electric push mowers for my yard. The house I'm trying to save from the bank, it has this beautiful little patch of grass in the front. It's perfect for a push mower. They're so quiet, you know? And better for the environment. I try to be eco-friendly when I can. I always bring my reusable bags to the grocery store. I have this whole collection of them in the trunk of my car. I got this one really cute bag from a farmer's market last summer, it has little hand-painted lemons all over it. The woman selling them said she paints them all herself. She had this huge stall with all these different fruits and vegetables painted on tote bags and aprons. I almost bought an apron with eggplants on it, but I don't really cook enough to justify wearing an apron. I mostly just make pasta or heat up leftovers. I make a really good baked ziti, though. The secret is to mix a little bit of cream cheese into the ricotta before you layer it. It makes it so creamy. My mom taught me that trick. She used to make it every year for my birthday when I was a kid. We would always have it with garlic bread and a big salad. 

But yeah, no, I'm not feeling depressed all day. Just normal, really.
Have you ever had times when the belief about the bank and your coworkers was present only when you were also feeling depressed or unusually high?

Only when I'm depressed or high? No, no, it's just... it's just always there. The bank stuff is happening regardless of my mood. It's not like a feeling, it's a fact, you know? They are actively trying to foreclose on my house, and my coworkers are involved in the paperwork. It doesn't matter if I'm happy or sad or just, you know, existing. 

Speaking of existing, I was just thinking about how expensive it is to just exist these days. Have you seen the price of eggs lately? It's outrageous. I went to the store yesterday and a dozen was like six dollars. Six dollars! For eggs! I used to eat eggs every morning for breakfast. Scrambled, with a little bit of hot sauce. I love that Cholula hot sauce, the one with the little wooden cap. It's not too spicy, it just has a really good flavor. I put it on everything. I even put it on my mac and cheese. 

My roommate in college used to think I was crazy for that. She would always make this fancy baked mac and cheese with like, four different kinds of Gruyere and breadcrumbs on top. She was going to culinary school, so she was always practicing her recipes on me. I gained like fifteen pounds my freshman year just from eating her cooking. She made this incredible chocolate lava cake once... I still think about that cake sometimes. It was so rich. 

But anyway, yeah, the bank thing is just a constant reality. It has nothing to do with my mood.

Speaking of paperwork, you wouldn't believe the stack of inventory sheets I have to sign off on at the store every single week. I supervise the sales floor, and the new cashiers they hire, they don't even know how to load the receipt tape anymore. I had this one girl last week, she jammed the main register three times before her lunch break. It's just exhausting trying to manage people who don't pay attention. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Right, the house. The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job—probably the ones messing up the registers on purpose—they’ve been quietly working together to push me out of my house. Irritable? Agitated? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I get annoyed sometimes, but who doesn't? He kept all the losing ones in a shoebox in his closet for some reason. I helped my aunt clean out his house after he passed away, and we found like... five shoeboxes just full of losing lottery tickets. It took us all afternoon to recycle them all. The recycling truck in my neighborhood comes so early now, too. If I don't put the bin out the night before, I always miss it. Read my thoughts? Oh, goodness, no. That sounds like something out of one of those science fiction movies my brother used to watch. If the people actually in the building are sweating, shouldn't we be able to turn the air up? But, no, no one can read my thoughts. I don't think that's even possible.

But anyway, yeah, the arguments. It's just exhausting. And at work, it's spilling over too. I've had a few really tense exchanges with the managers lately over just ordinary paperwork. They keep asking me to sign these forms, and I know what they're doing, so I push back. Now everyone is walking on eggshells around me. Jumbled? No, I don't think my thoughts are jumbled at all. I mean, everything I say makes perfect sense to me. I'm just trying to explain the whole picture, you know? My grandmother and I used to do those big 1,000-piece ones on her dining room table. She had this beautiful mahogany table that she kept covered with a plastic tablecloth so it wouldn't get scratched. We'd sit there for hours on Sunday afternoons. She always smelled like lavender and those little peppermint candies she kept in her purse. 

I still buy those peppermints sometimes, just for the nostalgia. They're getting harder to find, though. The grocery store down the street stopped carrying them. Withdraw? Stop working? No, I haven't stopped working. I mean, I still get up every morning, put on my uniform, and go in to supervise my team. I love cut glass. I have this gorgeous bowl on my dining table that I found at an antique shop in Vermont. We went there for our honeymoon, actually. The leaves were just starting to turn, all those brilliant reds and oranges. It was breathtaking. We stayed in this little bed and breakfast where they made fresh maple syrup.

That's when I have to stop and deal with it, because it's all connected. But if that's not happening, I'm just doing my normal routine. Like grocery shopping. I still go every Sunday. Although, I really need to find a new store, because like I said, they moved the peppermints, and now they've stopped carrying my favorite brand of coffee filters. The cone-shaped ones, you know? I had to buy a white noise machine, but it only has these weird settings like 'babbling brook' or 'summer night.' The summer night one has crickets, and who wants to sleep listening to crickets? It just makes me think there are bugs in the house. But no, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I see exactly what's going on.

patient.answer:
Unquestionably true? Yes, absolutely. I mean, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... just paperwork and missed payments, like it's some normal administrative thing. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. 

Speaking of papers, though, the documents they use at the bank are always printed on that really thick, heavy stock. We used to use paper like that for the promotional signage at my store, back before corporate made us switch to digital displays. I really hate the digital displays. The brightness gives me a headache, and the colors are never right. The red always looks a little bit orange, you know? Like a burnt sienna. I had a crayon that exact color when I was little, in the big box of 64 with the sharpener built into the back. I used to color for hours on the living room floor. My mom had this thick, green shag carpet, the kind you could lose a quarter in if you dropped it. My brother and I used to pretend it was a jungle for my plastic dinosaurs. The triceratops was always my favorite. I had a green one and a purple one, but the dog chewed up the purple one's tail. He was a golden retriever named Buster. Best dog we ever had, honestly. He used to wait for me by the front window every day after school.

patient.answer: Withdrawn? From other people? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still talk to people. I have to talk to people all day at work. But I guess I don't go out as much as I used to. It's just exhausting, you know? Dealing with everyone. Plus, going out costs so much money now. Have you seen the price of a movie ticket lately? It's outrageous. And the popcorn! They charge you like ten dollars for a bucket of popcorn, and they don't even use real butter anymore. It's some kind of weird, yellow oil. I remember when I was a teenager, I worked at the local theater for a summer. We had this big block of actual butter that we'd melt down. The smell was incredible. It would just permeate your clothes, though. I'd come home smelling like a walking concession stand. My mom used to make me leave my uniform in the garage because she said it was making the whole house smell like a carnival. We had this old, detached garage with a creaky wooden door. My dad spent a whole weekend trying to fix the track on that door once, but he ended up just making it worse. He was always trying to fix things himself instead of calling a professional. He tried to fix the plumbing under the kitchen sink once and ended up flooding the entire kitchen. The water ruined the linoleum. It was this awful, 70s-style yellow and brown pattern anyway, so I guess it was a blessing in disguise. But we had to eat takeout for a week while they replaced the floor. We got Chinese food from this place down the street, Golden Dragon. They had the best egg rolls. So crispy. But anyway, no, I don't think I'm withdrawn. I just prefer to stay home where it's quiet.

patient.answer: Depressed? Or high? No, no, my mood's been pretty normal, I think. I mean, as normal as you can be when people are actively trying to steal your home from you. But I haven't been like, crying in bed all day or bouncing off the walls. I've just been focused. You have to be focused when you're dealing with something like this. Speaking of focus, though, it's so hard to concentrate at work lately because they keep changing the layout of the store. Corporate sends down these new 'planograms' every month, and we have to move all the merchandise around. It's supposed to increase sales, but it just confuses the customers. Yesterday, this older lady spent twenty minutes looking for the travel-sized shampoo. We used to keep it right by the registers, which makes sense, right? People grab it on their way out. But now it's all the way in aisle four, next to the hair dye. I don't know who comes up with these ideas. Probably some guy in an office who's never actually worked retail a day in his life. My first retail job was at a pet store when I was in high school. I loved that job. I got to play with the puppies on my break. We had this one beagle mix, he had these huge floppy ears and he would just howl whenever the phone rang. It was the funniest thing. I wanted to adopt him so badly, but my mom said our house wasn't big enough for a dog. We lived in this little ranch-style house with a tiny backyard. The grass was always mostly crabgrass, no matter what my dad did to try and fix it. He bought all this expensive fertilizer and spent hours out there on the weekends, but it never looked like the lawns in the magazines. He was so proud of his lawnmower, though. It was a riding mower, bright red. He used to let me steer it when I was little, sitting on his lap. It smelled like gasoline and cut grass. I still love that smell. But anyway, no, my mood hasn't been unusually high or low. Just... dealing with things.

patient.answer: Seen things? Like hallucinations? No, no, I don't see things that aren't there. Just a mild prescription, but it makes a huge difference when I'm looking at the tiny print on the inventory sheets. I bought a pair of those cheap ones from the pharmacy, you know the ones that come in a three-pack? I got a blue pair, a red pair, and a tortoiseshell pair. The tortoiseshell ones are my favorite. They make me feel very... studious. Like a librarian. I always thought it would be nice to be a librarian. Just surrounded by books all day, quiet, organized. I used to go to the public library every Saturday when I was a kid. The children's section was in the basement, and it always smelled like old paper and floor wax. They had this big beanbag chair that was shaped like a hamburger. It was so faded and lumpy, but all the kids fought over who got to sit in it. I read all the Nancy Drew mysteries sitting in that hamburger chair. I loved Nancy Drew. She was so smart and independent, driving around in her blue roadster. I always wanted a convertible. Not blue, though. Maybe a cherry red one. With white leather seats. Although, white leather would be a nightmare to keep clean, especially if you spill coffee. I spilled coffee in my car just last week. It was one of those iced lattes, and it went right into the cup holder and got all sticky. patient.answer: Yeah, I mean, my mood is always normal when I'm thinking about it. Because it's just the reality of what's happening. I usually buy the instant packets, you know, the maple brown sugar kind? But I decided to try making it from scratch with the rolled oats. It takes longer, obviously, but it's supposed to be healthier. I added some sliced almonds and a little bit of honey. I got the honey from this farmer's market I went to last weekend. It was so crowded there. People everywhere, pushing strollers and walking their dogs. There was this one guy selling artisan cheeses, and he had samples out. I tried this smoked gouda that was amazing, but it was like fifteen dollars for a tiny wedge. I can't justify spending that much on cheese. But she acts like it's a federal offense. I think she just likes to hear herself talk, honestly. She wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she moves her arms. You can hear her coming from three aisles away. It reminds me of my middle school math teacher, Mrs. Gable. She wore a lot of jewelry, too. And she always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She was so strict. If you didn't show your work on a math problem, she'd mark the whole thing wrong, even if you got the right answer. I hated math. I was always more of an English student. I loved writing essays. So, yeah, my mood is fine. The stuff with the bank is just... it's just a fact of my life right now.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms occurred exclusively during mood episodes, which would favor a mood disorder with psychotic features rather than delusional disorder
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of several days or more when these beliefs were present only while your mood was very depressed or very high?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the relationship between the delusions and mood episodes (to rule out schizoaffective disorder or mood disorders with psychotic features), which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
No, it's never been like that. It's not tied to being depressed or high, because I'm not either of those things. The situation with the bank is just always happening, regardless of my mood. I mean, my mood is pretty steady. Unless I haven't had my morning tea, I guess. I switched from coffee to green tea a few months ago because the acid in coffee was just killing my stomach. Plus, green tea has all those antioxidants. 

I buy the loose leaf kind from this little shop downtown. They have all these giant glass jars lining the walls, it looks like an old apothecary. The owner is this sweet older man who always gives me a free sample of a new blend. Last time he gave me this peach hibiscus one. It was bright pink when it brewed. It tasted a little like potpourri, honestly, but I drank it anyway. I hate wasting things. I'm the kind of person who will scrape the very bottom of the peanut butter jar with a spatula. My roommate in college used to just throw the jar away when there was still a good two tablespoons left! It drove me crazy. We did not get along very well. She was a theater major and was always doing vocal warm-ups at like, six in the morning. 'Red leather, yellow leather,' over and over. 

I was taking a lot of early classes so I was already awake, but still. I took this one art history class that was fascinating, though. We spent a whole month just on the Renaissance. The paintings from that era are so incredibly detailed. I always wonder how they got the fabric to look so realistic, like you could just reach out and touch the velvet. I have a velvet throw pillow on my couch, actually. It's emerald green. I got it on sale at HomeGoods. I love HomeGoods, you never know what you're going to find there. I went in for a picture frame once and came out with a giant ceramic owl. But anyway, no, my mood doesn't really have anything to do with what's going on.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the fixed belief is actually bizarre or delusional in nature, which best separates delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis
doctor.question: Have you ever thought that some outside force is directly controlling your thoughts or actions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of control (outside forces controlling thoughts or actions), which is not covered by the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Controlling my thoughts? No, no, I'm the one in charge of my own brain. Nobody is like... pulling strings or forcing me to do things. Well, except my store manager, but that's just her being a total micromanager. She tries to control everything I do on the floor. Like yesterday, she completely redid the associate schedule after I had already finalized it. And I had spent an hour color-coding it! 

I use those really nice gel pens, you know the ones that don't bleed through the paper? I have a set of thirty-six colors. I keep them in this little mesh pouch I found in the dollar spot at Target. Target is so dangerous, honestly. You go in for toothpaste and you come out with a new bathmat, three candles, and a bag of pretzels. I love those peanut butter filled pretzels. They're so salty and crunchy. I try not to buy them too often though, because I will literally sit on the couch and eat half the tub while watching HGTV. I love those home renovation shows. It's amazing how they can take a house that looks like a total dump and turn it into this beautiful open-concept thing in like, thirty minutes of television. I always want to knock down a wall in my apartment after I watch them, but I'm pretty sure my landlord would evict me. He's this grumpy guy who complains if you even put a nail in the wall to hang a picture. So I just use those Command hooks for everything. They really do work, as long as you pull the tab straight down when you take them off. If you pull it towards you, it rips the paint right off the drywall. I learned that the hard way in my last place. 

But yeah, no, my thoughts are just my own. No outside forces or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia spectrum psychosis by assessing functional decline
doctor.question: Have you noticed a clear decline in your work performance because of these beliefs?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's work performance and functioning, specifically whether it has been impaired by the beliefs, which maps to the criterion that functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion.

patient.answer:
Well, no, not really a decline. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't involved, I still get up for work every day, I supervise my team, handle the schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself just fine. 

Like just yesterday, I had to deal with this woman trying to return a blender without a receipt. It didn't even have our store brand on it, but she was screaming at me that she bought it here. I just stayed calm, you know? Put on my customer service voice. I actually used to work in food service back when I was getting my associate's degree, and that really teaches you patience. People get so incredibly mad if you forget their extra ranch dressing. It's wild. The things people will yell over. 

But anyway, yeah, I do my job. The problems mostly just start when there's mail, or if the bank calls, or if the workplace paperwork seems tied to what I believe is happening with the house. Then it's... well, it's hard to ignore. 

Speaking of paperwork, our printer in the back office is always jamming. It’s this massive, ancient gray thing that sounds like an airplane taking off when it prints. I’ve put in like three maintenance requests for it, but corporate just tells us to clean the rollers with rubbing alcohol. Have you ever tried to reach inside a commercial printer? I always get black toner all over my hands and my cuffs. And it does not wash off easily. You have to scrub it with that gritty pumice soap, the orange kind mechanics use. My dad used to keep a giant bottle of that by the sink in the garage. He was always tinkering with his old Chevy truck. He loved that truck more than anything, I swear he waxed it every single Sunday afternoon... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my work. Yeah, my performance is totally fine as long as the bank and the house stuff isn't popping up in my paperwork.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed belief is a mood-congruent psychotic symptom occurring during a major depressive episode versus a delusional disorder with no major mood episode.
doctor.question: During this time, have you also been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of depression (feeling depressed most of the day, nearly every day), which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Depressed? No, I don't think so. I don't feel sad or down all day, if that's what you mean. I get up, I go to work, I do my thing. I mean, I have my moments of being annoyed, obviously, but not depressed. Like this morning, I was so annoyed because my neighbor decided to mow his lawn at 7 AM. Who does that on a weekday? And he has one of those gas mowers that sounds like a lawnmower and a chainsaw had a baby. It's so loud. 

I actually really want to get one of those electric push mowers for my yard. The house I'm trying to save from the bank, it has this beautiful little patch of grass in the front. It's perfect for a push mower. They're so quiet, you know? And better for the environment. I try to be eco-friendly when I can. I always bring my reusable bags to the grocery store. I have this whole collection of them in the trunk of my car. I got this one really cute bag from a farmer's market last summer, it has little hand-painted lemons all over it. The woman selling them said she paints them all herself. She had this huge stall with all these different fruits and vegetables painted on tote bags and aprons. I almost bought an apron with eggplants on it, but I don't really cook enough to justify wearing an apron. I mostly just make pasta or heat up leftovers. I make a really good baked ziti, though. The secret is to mix a little bit of cream cheese into the ricotta before you layer it. It makes it so creamy. My mom taught me that trick. She used to make it every year for my birthday when I was a kid. We would always have it with garlic bread and a big salad. 

But yeah, no, I'm not feeling depressed all day. Just normal, really.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the psychotic symptoms are confined to a mood episode, which would support a mood disorder with psychotic features rather than delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had times when the belief about the bank and your coworkers was present only when you were also feeling depressed or unusually high?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the delusions only occur during mood episodes (depressed or unusually high/manic). The symptom profile does not contain information about the relationship between the delusions and mood episodes.

patient.answer:
Only when I'm depressed or high? No, no, it's just... it's just always there. The bank stuff is happening regardless of my mood. It's not like a feeling, it's a fact, you know? They are actively trying to foreclose on my house, and my coworkers are involved in the paperwork. It doesn't matter if I'm happy or sad or just, you know, existing. 

Speaking of existing, I was just thinking about how expensive it is to just exist these days. Have you seen the price of eggs lately? It's outrageous. I went to the store yesterday and a dozen was like six dollars. Six dollars! For eggs! I used to eat eggs every morning for breakfast. Scrambled, with a little bit of hot sauce. I love that Cholula hot sauce, the one with the little wooden cap. It's not too spicy, it just has a really good flavor. I put it on everything. I even put it on my mac and cheese. 

My roommate in college used to think I was crazy for that. She would always make this fancy baked mac and cheese with like, four different kinds of Gruyere and breadcrumbs on top. She was going to culinary school, so she was always practicing her recipes on me. I gained like fifteen pounds my freshman year just from eating her cooking. She made this incredible chocolate lava cake once... I still think about that cake sometimes. It was so rich. 

But anyway, yeah, the bank thing is just a constant reality. It has nothing to do with my mood.

opening_question.intent: Establish the chief concern to guide the diagnostic interview.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you’re here. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion involving the bank, loan servicer, and coworkers conspiring to force foreclosure, present continuously for almost two years, with preserved functioning outside the delusional theme and no hallucinations, thought disorder, or mood episode. This best fits persistent delusional disorder rather than an organic psychotic disorder.
